title: Proper pushforward of extension by zero
statement:
For every datum in
the comparison-map
construction, the specified map $\alpha_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix a datum of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]: schemes $u:T_1\to T_2$ proper, open immersions $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ with $uj_1=j_2$, a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, and $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Put $M=Ru_*j_{1!}K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], the section $s:X\to V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$ has clopen image and $ps=\mathrm{id}_X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification], the specified composite $\theta:j_2^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is an isomorphism. The definition specifies $\alpha=\varepsilon_M\circ j_{2!}(\theta^{-1})$. On sheaves, the counit is induced by the identity on every etale object factoring through $X$, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]; restriction therefore identifies $j_2^{-1}\varepsilon_M$ with the identity on $j_2^{-1}M$. Likewise $j_2^{-1}j_{2!}K$ identifies with $K$: on an etale object over $X$, the extension-by-zero presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is exactly the original sheaf. Every etale object and every member of a covering over an object factoring through $X$ also factors through $X$. On this restricted site the presheaf is already a sheaf, so its sheafification and the sheafified counit retain those identities. These identities hold termwise and descend with the adjunction as specified in the comparison definition. Consequently $j_2^{-1}\alpha$ is $\theta^{-1}$ under this identification, and is an isomorphism. It is not necessary to call this map an identity without specifying the theta identification.

proof.text: Let $\bar z:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_2$ have image outside $j_2(X)$ and put $F=T_1\times_{T_2}P$, $i:F\to T_1$ and $a:F\to P$. The pullback $X\times_{T_1}F$ is empty: any point of it would map under $uj_1=j_2$ both into $j_2(X)$ and to the image of $\bar z$, a contradiction. Thus the square with right open immersion $j_1$, bottom map $i$, and left open immersion $\varnothing\hookrightarrow F$ is an open-immersion square of [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Applying [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] gives $i^{-1}j_{1!}K\simeq(\varnothing\hookrightarrow F)_!(K|_{\varnothing})=0$. Indeed the only sheaf of modules on the empty scheme's small etale site is zero (the empty covering forces its sections on the empty object to be zero), hence every complex there is zero; alternatively the extension-by-zero presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is zero on every nonempty etale object, and is zero also on the empty object. This proves vanishing of the actual module complex on the fibre, without assuming a stalk formula is part of the definition.

proof.text: The proper map $u$, finite ring $\Lambda$, and bounded-below object $j_{1!}K$ satisfy [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]. Bounded-below extension by zero is part of the comparison datum, and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] also gives its termwise exact realization. The first, derived formula of the corollary gives $\bar z^{-1}M\simeq Ra_*i^{-1}j_{1!}K=0$ by step 2; an additive derived direct-image functor carries the zero complex to zero. On the source, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], clause 2, says that every term of $j_{2!}K$ has zero stalk at $\bar z$. Hence its termwise stalk complex is zero. These assertions include an empty fibre and make no finiteness or constructibility assumption on the individual sheaves of $K$.

proof.text: For every integer $q$, stalks commute with cohomology: the underlying abelian stalk functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] supplies $H^q(FN)\simeq F H^q(N)$ for any exact functor $F$. The inverse image of module sheaves is exact and agrees with underlying abelian inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. At $\bar z:P\to T_2$, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] identifies the underlying stalk with $\Gamma(P,\bar z^{-1}(-))$ and makes $\Gamma(P,-)$ exact, also for modules. Thus step 3 implies that both $\mathcal H^q(j_{2!}K)_{\bar z}$ and $\mathcal H^q(M)_{\bar z}$ vanish off $j_2(X)$. For a point in $j_2(X)$, restriction identifies pointed etale neighbourhoods inside that open with neighbourhoods in $X$ (intersect any neighbourhood with the open); therefore its stalk is the stalk of the restricted sheaf. Exactness of restriction and step 1 make the stalk of $\mathcal H^q(\alpha)$ an isomorphism there. Off the open it is the unique map $0\to0$, also an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian sheaf morphism of $\mathcal H^q(\alpha)$ for each $q$, using step 4. Each is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves, hence of $\Lambda$-module sheaves: if a linear map $h$ has inverse $v$ on abelian sheaves, then $h(v(\lambda y))=\lambda y=h(\lambda v(y))$, so injectivity gives $v(\lambda y)=\lambda v(y)$ on every object. Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] with the abelian category $\Mod(T_{2,\Et},\Lambda)$, not the pro-etale category and not merely abelian coefficients. Every cohomology map of $\alpha$ is invertible, so the specified $\alpha_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(T_{2,\Et},\Lambda)$.
